newsitem.title: UK: Britain's casinos revel in new freedom.
newsitem.headline: Britain's casinos revel in new freedom.

text.p: Britain's casino operators sighed with relief on Thursday when the government relaxed some tough curbs, allowing establishments to admit new members more quickly and keep bars open later.
Casinos had argued that rules introduced 30 years ago had to be relaxed to allow them to cope with increased competition from overseas gambling centres and the success of Britain's National Lottery.
The time a gambler has to wait between applying to join a casino and gaming at its tables is cut to 24 hours from 48.
The new rules will also free casinos from operating "pub hours" in their bars, allowing them to remain open until 2 a.m. in the provinces and 3 a.m. in London.
The casino industry had argued that the waiting time for new members discouraged business executives and tourists in Britain for only a few days from visiting their tables.
Later this month casino punters in Britain will be allowed to use debit cards as well as cash and cheques.
The British Casino Association (BCA), which represents the country's 117 licensed casinos, welcomed the reforms but said more had to be done to help the industry.

"We hope that the...much-needed additional reforms, which are so necessary to buttress the health and competitiveness of the industry, will be undertaken as a matter of some urgency," general secretary Brian Lemon said in a statement.
The BCA is pressing for an end to a ban on casinos advertising their services and also wants new laws to allow three slot machines to be installed per gaming table.
Tom Kavanagh, secretary to the Gaming Board which regulates the gambling industry, said when Britain first allowed casino betting it aimed to stop the pastime from becoming too popular.

"The casinos were allowed to meet the need which existed but were not allowed to stimulate it," he said by telephone. "But these laws were passed 30 years ago and the whole world has moved on since then."
The government said last year that further consideration was needed before proposals to allow casinos in 21 new locations could go ahead.
